summary: U Dhammissara is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed a Master of Arts at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under supervisor Sanu Mahatthanadull, attested in 2017.
Ugyen Pelgen works in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He earned a master's degree from Aligarh Muslim University and served as a lecturer of history at Sherubtse College.

Ulrich Pagel specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Tadeusz Skorupski, Philip Denwood, and Renate Söhnen-Thieme, and held a post at SOAS University of London (attested 2013-2020).

Ulrich Timme Kragh works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Karmapa International Buddhist Institute and the University of Copenhagen, later holding posts at Copenhagen, Geumgang University, Harvard, IIAS, the University of Sydney, and Australian National University.

Ulrich von Wilamowitz-Moellendorff was a scholar of linguistics and history and archaeology. Educated at Schulpforta, Bonn, and Berlin under Otto Jahn, Moriz Haupt, and others, he held professorships at Greifswald, Göttingen (1883-1897), and Berlin (1897-1921).

Ulrike Roesler is a Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her PhD at the University of Münster. She taught at Freiburg and Marburg, and held posts at the University of Oxford, Wolfson College, Oxford, and the Pali Text Society.

Uma Chakravarti is a historian and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Mount Carmel College, Banaras Hindu University, and the University of Delhi under D. Devahuti. She served as an educator at Miranda House from 1966 to 1998.

Umakant Premanand Shah was a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. At Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda, he served as deputy director in 1954 and head of the Ramayana Project in 1965.

Unnikrishnan Payyappallimana works in Indology and related fields. He studied at Ayurveda College, Coimbatore and the University of Amsterdam, later holding research and teaching posts at FRLHT, Amala Institute of Medical Sciences, and the University of Toyama.

Unrai Wogihara was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Taisho University and the University of Strasbourg under Ernst Leumann. He taught at the University of Tokyo and Taisho University, and served as principal of Shiba Junior & Senior High School.
Unsho Shaku was an active figure in Buddhist studies who studied at Mount Koya in 1844. He founded the Kairitsu Gakko and, in 1884, established the Juzenkai.

Uranchimeg Borjigd Ujeed is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She earned her PhD from SOAS University of London and held a post as a research associate at the University of Cambridge.

Uranchimeg Tsultem works in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. Educated at MNUAC, Eötvös Loránd University, and UC Berkeley (PhD), she held positions at MNUAC, UC Berkeley, National University of Mongolia, IUPUI, and Indiana University Bloomington.

Urs App is a scholar in Buddhist, religious, and computational studies who earned his PhD from Temple University and studied at Fribourg and Kyoto. He held posts at Hanazono University, the International Research Institute for Zen Buddhism, and EFEO.

Usha Nilsson was an Indology and linguistics scholar. She spent her career at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where she was a faculty member (attested 2001) and later Emeritus Professor of Languages and Cultures of Asia (attested 2026).
Uta Reinöhl is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. She held a post at the University of Cologne in 2018 and assumed the Chair of General Linguistics at the University of Freiburg in 2026.

Ute Hüsken is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her doctorate at the University of Göttingen under Heinz Bechert. She held posts at Göttingen, Heidelberg University, and the University of Oslo (2007-2017).

Utz Podzeit was an Indologist who completed his Dr. phil. at the University of Vienna. He served as a university lecturer in Indology at Vienna beginning in 1969 and conducted research at the University of Madras from 1972 to 1974.

V. Kameswari is an Indologist affiliated with the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, where she served as an Editorial Committee member (attested 2001) and as a supervisor and guide (attested 2026).

V. P. Bhatta is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. At Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, he served as head of the Sanskrit Dictionary Project (attested 2011) and as Professor-Editor for the Sanskrit Dictionary (attested 2026).
